Hi Samantha / Jared,

Thanks again for the time today — really appreciate the walkthrough of Acme's clinical summarization flow and the throughput requirements you mentioned (bursty traffic during EOD processing, steady 30 TPS average with 3x peak windows). Quick recap + next steps below: 

- Recap: you need an extractive+abstractive summarization pipeline with high accuracy on clinical notes, strict PII handling, and predictable latency (p95 target under 250ms for 512-token responses).
- Model recommendations (initial): rw-instruct-13b-v2 (good cost/quality), rw-7b-quant (for lower-cost routing), and Redwood-Llama-70b-quant (for best-in-class quality on long contexts).
- Action items: I attached the initial benchmark PDF and our prompt set v1 for your QA to review. Would love permission to run a short, non-production perf window against your sample dataset next week to validate TPS/latency numbers on our Dedicated pool.

Thanks, Dylan — helpful recap. A couple of quick clarifications before we schedule the perf window: 

1) The p95 and p99 numbers in your PDF look great for rw-instruct-13b-v2, but can you confirm p99 (or p99.9 if you have it) for the 512-token case at 30 TPS? Our compliance team focuses on tail latency for SLA. 

2) Cost sensitivity — can you give a rough order-of-magnitude cost delta between rw-instruct-13b-v2 and rw-7b-quant for our expected monthly volume (approx. 10M tokens/day)?

3) Security: we'll need confirmation that the perf run will not persist any PHI and that logs from the trial can be scoped/filtered — Jared, can you loop in security if needed.

If those answers look good we can do a short test next week. Monday morning is tight for us; Tue afternoon looks better.

—Samantha

Samantha — thanks for the questions. Quick answers inline and a short summary of Redwood-verified numbers from the benchmark PDF / dashboard.

1) Tail latency (512 tokens, 30 TPS): our verified profile for rw-instruct-13b-v2 on nvidia-a100: p50=110ms, p95=190ms, p99=280ms. p99.9 is ~410ms in our Dedicated config; that drops ~10-15% on burst-optimized GPU pools. For rw-7b-quant: p50=65ms, p95=110ms, p99=160ms. (All numbers measured with continuous batching enabled and your prompt sets.)

2) Cost delta (rough): on a 10M tokens/day workload, estimated monthly inference cost: rw-instruct-13b-v2 ~= $34k/month; rw-7b-quant ~= $12k/month. We include caching and batching assumptions in the attached PDF and the dashboard has the per-token breakdown. We'll run your prompt_set_v1 against both models in the perf window to give exact numbers.

3) Security: the perf run can be scoped to your redacted dataset (you can provide a masked sample) and we'll disable persistent logging of input content for the test. We'll produce scoped telemetry (latency/tps/error rates) and a sanitized trace for your security team. If you want a brief security checklist, I can share our standard perf-run controls.

Recommended approach: start with rw-7b-quant as the baseline for most traffic, with a canary for rw-instruct-13b-v2 on 10-15% of requests targeting higher-quality summarization. For very high-fidelity cases, Redwood-Llama-70b-quant can be used as a fallback in the routing policy.

Proposed perf window: Tue 2026-06-22 02:00-06:00 UTC (we'll adjust to your timezone). Can you confirm availability? If yes, we'll need a 20–30 minute pre-test sync to nail dataset and success criteria.

Attachments referenced: [Attachment: redwood_benchmark_acme_20260618.pdf], [Attachment: prompt_set_v1.jsonl]

Dashboard (selected metrics):
- Model: rw-instruct-13b-v2 | Throughput (sustained): 30 TPS | p50=110ms | p95=190ms | p99=280ms | tokens/sec per GPU: ~225
- Model: rw-7b-quant | Throughput (sustained): 60 TPS | p50=65ms | p95=110ms | p99=160ms | tokens/sec per GPU: ~420

Let me know if you'd like me to include marissa or rishi on the pre-sync.

Best,
Dylan
